claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and the children you're inquiring about.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about just one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son, Alex.

Now, to help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 18 years old. He was born in March 2007.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18 years old, I need to understand his current circumstances to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He finished school and isn't doing anything like that right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question to help assess Alex's eligibility:

**Are you a UK resident, and do you have responsibility for Alex?** (For example, is he living with you, or are you his main carer?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to make a determination regarding Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me explain the situation:

Alex is 18 years old and is not in full-time education or an approved training scheme. According to UK Child Benefit rules, eligibility generally ends when a child reaches 16, unless they are in full-time education or an approved training scheme. Since Alex has finished school and is not currently pursuing either of these options, he would not qualify for Child Benefit.

Additionally, even though you are a UK resident with responsibility for Alex and he lives with you, the age and education/training requirements are the key factors that determine eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. The key reason is that while you meet the residency and responsibility requirements, Alex's age and current circumstances mean he doesn't qualify.

If Alex were to start full-time education or an approved training scheme in the future, his eligibility status could potentially change. If you have any other questions about this or your circumstances change, please feel free to reach out.
